description:
AI agents are writing massive amounts of code, but human reviewers are drowning in the backlog. Today, we look at how to fix the bottleneck, why Google is killing its own coding agent, and how to actually hold these autonomous systems accountable.

Alex, Jamie, and Rufus debate the biggest artificial intelligence news from the last 24–48 hours, with three distinct stories, competing perspectives and practical takeaways.

What we covered:
• LinearB launches 'Agentic Studio' to manage AI agent workflows
• Ebix and intentyx partner to launch SMARE for AI agent governance
• Google to shutter AI coding agent Jules by year-end

What changed. Who wins. What you do next.

The Edge: what changed, who wins, who is exposed, and what to watch next.

Listener question: When an AI tool you rely on gets shut down, what's your biggest concern?

title_candidates_v3_3.listener_promise: You will understand the new tools for managing AI code bloat, how to audit autonomous agents, and why you need to back up your AI session data now.

positions.alex: Believes we are in a 'growing pains' phase where we have to build the tools to manage the agents we've already unleashed.
positions.jamie: Argues that we are rushing to build 'safety' and 'efficiency' layers that are really just new ways to hide the fact that we don't fully understand how these agents work.
positions.rufus: Observes that the market is currently paying for the 'infrastructure of control' because it's the only way to keep the AI boom going without a catastrophic failure.

concession.gives_ground_on: The necessity of audit trails for AI agents in highly regulated industries like finance.

title_candidates_v3_3.who_wins: The engineering managers who prioritize governance over raw speed.
title_candidates_v3_3.who_is_exposed: Developers who haven't backed up their AI-assisted workflows.
title_candidates_v3_3.normal_person_payoff: You'll save yourself a headache by exporting your AI chat history before the next big platform consolidation.

mandatory_receipts: AI-assisted pull requests are 2.6 times larger and take 5x longer to review.
